Keep Heilprin’s proposed correction qualified. The directly checked Ketubot gives Rabbah, while Gittin 26b gives Abba in a parallel chain.
The first name and the end of the chain vary. Gittin 81b identifies Rabbah bar Sheilta and Adda bar Ahavah. Heilprin’s abridged wording keeps Abba visible.
The chronological statement is Heilprin’s reading. The Zohar Introduction describes Shimon’s vision. Its narrative alone does not date this Hamnuna historically.
Heilprin’s Devarim locator differs from the checked placement. The near-verbatim narrator, companions and Sikhnin are attested in the Balak chapter.

The escort and prior deaths remain a characterization within Heilprin. Idra Zuta announces each presence separately and narrates Shimon’s last teaching. Heilprin’s Shimon entry repeats the escort claim.
The exact underlying incident is located; the printed siglum remains unclear. The Vilna-style folio markers in the checked transcription place Elijah’s explanation at 144b.
Heilprin’s inference remains unadjudicated. The checked Bavli and Zohar records support distinct genres and report chains. Tosafot distinguishes two Talmudic Hamnunas by teachers.

The scope of the alleged omission requires a direct reading. The exact Sheerit Yosef passage was not established. Zacuto’s directly read notice discusses distinctions among Talmudic Hamnunas without settling Heilprin’s two-Elders claim.
The exact printed Emek HaMelekh passage remains a collation hold. A catalogue and a facsimile were located. The facsimile retrieval exceeded the source tool’s limit, so the exact folio was not read.
